scope: Storage and microkernel audit only; no training or unseen classification dataset is used
baseline: Native dense virtual vector 1210 FP16 coefficients stored in a 22-byte-header raw file, then FP64 matrix execution
mirror_storage: 768 FP16 physical coefficients + ceil(1210/8) bitset + same 22-byte header, K=8,R=4 metadata
roundtrip: Load only physical coefficients and addresses, regenerate virtual 1210-vector with unchanged MA1164 source/core.py, compare exact FP16-quantized decoder predictions
implicit_execution: 128/256/64-wide sign-Hadamard Mirror; one shared physical vector; K=1,4; R=1,4; FP64 CPU batch64; no full virtual W allocation in direct path
checks: Q^-1 diag(u) Q direct vs dense equality
nonlinear Q^-1 tanh(diag(u) Qx) equality and nonzero gradient

timing.device: AMD EPYC virtual CPU, no GPU

hypotheses.storage: Stream-compatible physical state can be shorter than equivalent raw FP16 1210 dense weights
hypotheses.execution: K orthogonal views and R updates can be executed without persistent or temporary d-by-d virtual matrices for structured Mirror families
hypotheses.speed: CPU eager may not win; measured objectively

reproducibility: Source and RNG seeds fixed; task data none. Includes full input/output equality tests. Historical MA-1164 fresh data not reopened.
exclusions: No exact memory watermark; temporary vector workspace does exist
No GPU, fused CUDA kernel or arbitrary dense matrix equivalence
Runtime/code distribution bytes are common library costs and excluded symmetrically from raw per-model state files
